ORDER
PER HON’BLE MR. VIRENDER BHAT, JUDICIAL MEMBER
1. Review of common judgement dated 24th June, 2025 passed
by this Tribunal in Appeal Nos. 116 of 2023 & 177 of 2023 is sought
by way of this Review Petition.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R.P. No. 2 of 2026 Page 2 of 14

2. Both these appeals had been filed by the Review Petitioner
before this Tribunal challenging the orders dated 11th June, 2022 and
29th August, 2022 passed by the 1st Respondent – Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission (hereinafter referred to as “the Commission”)
in petition Nos. 9/TT/2021 and 583/MP/2020 respectively. By way of
these impugned orders, the Central Commission had held the Review
Petitioner, a solar park, liable to pay transmission charges for the
delay in commissioning of solar power projects situated within the
solar park.
3. In the common judgement under review dated 24th June, 2025,
this Tribunal held both these appeals sans any merit and accordingly
were dismissed.
4. We have heard Mr. Arijit Maitra, Learned Counsel for the
Review Petitioner, Ms. Swapna Seshadri, Learned Counsel for 2nd
Respondent (PGCIL) and Ms. Anisha Upadhyay, Learned Counsel
for 4th Respondent (CTUIL). We have also perused the written
submissions filed by the Learned Counsels.
5. According to the Review Petitioner, the said judgement dated
24th June, 2025 of this Tribunal suffers from errors apparent on the
face of record as :-
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R.P. No. 2 of 2026 Page 3 of 14

(a) This Tribunal has not considered the contention of
the Review Petitioner that the Commission had not
granted any hearing to it before passing the order
dated 11th June, 2022 in petition No. 9/TT/2021;
(b) this Tribunal has not followed its earlier decisions;
(c) this Tribunal has arrived at incorrect findings based
on incorrect facts;
(d) this Tribunal has ignored the fact that the
undertaking dated 23rd November, 2015 given by the
Review Petitioner was a conditional one; and
(e) this Tribunal has erred in not adding the solar power
generators as party to this appeal.
Our Analysis
(a) This Tribunal has not considered the contention of the
Review Petitioner that the Commission has not granted any
hearing to it before passing the order dated 11th June, 2022 in
petition No. 9/TT/2021;
&
(e) This Tribunal has erred in not adding the solar power
generators as party to this appeal:
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R.P. No. 2 of 2026 Page 4 of 14

6. It is true that one of the grounds of challenge to the impugned
orders raised by the Review Petitioner in the appeal was that the
order dated 11th June, 2022 suffers from judicial impropriety and has
been passed in violation of natural justice for the reason that no
opportunity of hearing was afforded to the Review Petitioner .
7. We may note that apart from the above ground of appeal,
several other grounds had also been raised by the Appellant in the
two appeals to assail the impugned orders dated 11th June, 2022 and
29th August, 2022. However, on 9th November, 2023, Learned
Counsel for Review Petitioner/Appellant submitted before this
Tribunal that the Appellant would confine its submissions in these
appeals only to its claims of not being liable to pay transmission
charges and any grievance, which it may have vis-à-vis the solar
power generators, would be resolved through the process of dispute
resolution as stipulated in their agreement and not claim against the
solar power generators would be agitated in these appeals. It is on
the basis of such submissions that the Learned Counsel for the
Appellant/Review Petitioner the solar power generators (Respondent
No. 3 in Appeal No. 116 of 2023 and Respondent Nos. 4 & 5 in appeal
No. 177 of 2023) were deleted from the array of Respondents as
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R.P. No. 2 of 2026 Page 5 of 14

sought by way of application Nos. 2275 of 2023 & 2276 of 2023. Thus,
the Appellants/Review Petitioners themselves had confined the
scope of the appeals to only one issue relating to their liability to pay
transmission charges and for this reason neither were remaining
issues/grounds raised in the two appeals argued by the Learned
Counsels nor were considered by this Tribunal vide writing the
judgement under review.
8. In view of the same, we find it intriguing to hear from the Review
Petitioner that their ground of challenge to the impugned order dated
11th June, 2022 that the same has been passed in violation of
principle of natural justice, has not been considered and discussed in
the judgement under review.
9. Similarly, once the Review Petitioner itself had sought deletion
of solar power generators from the array of respondents in these two
appeals, it cannot be heard to contend now in this Review Petition
that this Tribunal committed any error in not impleading the solar
power generators as party to the two appeals. The contentions of the
Review Petitioner in this regard in this Review Petition are patently
malafide, baseless and concocted. In view of such fictitious
statements having been made to create a false ground for review of
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R.P. No. 2 of 2026 Page 6 of 14

judgement dated 24th June, 2025, the Review Petitioner deserved to
be burdened with heavy cost.
(b) This Tribunal has not followed its earlier decisions :
10. It is submitted by the Learned Counsel for the Review Petitioner
that the judgement under review dated 24th June, 2025 is contrary to
the law laid down by this Tribunal in its previous judgement dated 21st
December, 2021 in Appeal No. 69 of 2021 of M/s Saurya Urja
Company of Rajasthan Ltd. Vs. RERC & Ors. Thus, it is contended
that the judgement under review suffers from a patent error which
needs to be rectified.
11. In this regard, we find it necessary to refer paragraph Nos. 75
to 78 of the judgement under review. In paragraph No. 75, this
Tribunal has clearly noted that the reliance of the Appellant upon the
judgment in Appeal No. 69 of 2021 is misconceived as the regulatory
provisions on the basis of which said judgement was rendered were
different from the regulatory provisions which are applicable to the
instant case. Thereafter, in paragraph Nos. 76 & 77, it has been
explained as to why the said judgement in Appeal No. 69 of 2021 is
not applicable to the factual matrix involved in the present appeal.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R.P. No. 2 of 2026 Page 7 of 14

12. Therefore, it does not lie in the mouth of the Review Petitioner
to contend that this Tribunal has not followed its previous decision
and the judgement under review suffers from any error apparent on
this ground.
(c) This Tribunal has arrived at incorrect findings based on
incorrect facts :
13. During the submission on this aspect, Learned Counsel for
Review Petitioner has drawn our attention to paragraph No. 98 of the
judgement under review which is extracted hereinbelow :-
“98. The submission that the undertaking is void under
Section 25 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, for want of
consideration, is misconceived. In public law contractual
frameworks, consideration is not limited to pecuniary
exchange but extends to benefits received in kind or
through legal facilitation. In this case, SUCRL has drawn
the power to apply for and secure connectivity for 500 MW
of capacity, avoiding the regulatory complexity and delays
that would otherwise arise if each generator were to apply
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R.P. No. 2 of 2026 Page 8 of 14

independently. That facilitation itself constitutes a valid
legal consideration.”
(Emphasis supplied)
14. Learned Counsel would argue that this Tribunal has incorrectly
noted in the said paragraph that the Appellant has drawn power to
apply for and to secure connectivity for 500MW capacity whereas the
Appellant has not drawn any power rather its evacuation system was
connected to ISTS. It is submitted that since there is neither any
auxiliary consumption nor start up power being used by the Appellant,
the question of the Appellant drawing any power does not arise in the
facts of the present case. Learned Counsel would argue that since
the judgement under review is based upon such incorrect facts, the
same deserved to be reviewed.
15. We are not impressed by the submissions made on behalf of
the Review Petitioner as the same are based upon absolutely
incorrect interpretation of the contents of paragraph No. 98 which has
been reproduced herein above. By the expression “SUCRL has
drawn the power to apply for and secure connectivity”, this Tribunal
did not mean the drawing of electricity from the generation units in the
solar park. What this Tribunal meant was that the Appellant had
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R.P. No. 2 of 2026 Page 9 of 14

empowered itself to apply for and secure connectivity for 500 MW of
capacity on behalf of the solar power generators in the solar park
thereby avoiding the regulatory complexity and delays that would
otherwise have been caused if each generator was to apply for
connectivity independently. Therefore, this ground of review also is
completely devoid of any merit.
(d) This Tribunal has ignored the fact that the undertaking
dated 23rd November, 2015 given by the Review Petitioner
was a conditional one:
16. Learned Counsel for the Review Petitioner would argue that
this Tribunal, while passing the judgement under review upon the
Appellant’s undertaking dated 23rd November, 2015 to bear all
liabilities related to connectivity/LTA has lost sight of the fact that the
undertaking was conditional as the same was given by the Appellant
“in accordance with CERC Regulations/orders” which fact has not
been considered by this Tribunal. According to the Learned Counsel,
this constituted an error apparent on the face of record in the
judgement under review and, therefore, needs to be rectified in this
Review Petition.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R.P. No. 2 of 2026 Page 10 of 14

17. On this aspect, we find it apposite to refer to paragraph Nos. 63
to 65 of the judgement under review which are extracted
hereinbelow:-
“63. In furtherance of this role, SUCRL furnished an
undertaking on 23.11.2015 to bear “all liabilities related
to connectivity/LTA in accordance with CERC
Regulations/orders on behalf of the Solar Power
Generators to be set up in the above Solar Park.” This
undertaking, SUCRL contends, was simply a pre-condition
for the grant of Connectivity and LTA, without import of
ongoing financial liability. The relevant extract of the
undertaking given by SUCRL is quoted as under:
“The company "Saurya Urja Company of Rajasthan
Limited" as Solar Power Park Developer for 500 MW Solar
Park, undertakes to bear all liabilities related to
connectivity /LTA in accordance with CERC
Regulations/ orders on behalf of the Solar power
generators to be set up in the above Solar park.”
64. From the above, it is beyond any doubt that all the
liabilities falling upon the Solar Power Generators in
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R.P. No. 2 of 2026 Page 11 of 14

accordance with CERC Regulations or Orders shall be
borne by the SUCRL.
65. Even if it is assumed that the SUCRL is an agent of
the Solar Power Generators, it cannot now be argued
that it has no liability for the payment of charges on
behalf of the Solar Power Generators, once it has
taken the responsibility under the contractual
agreements signed by it to the payees (PGCIL/CTUIL),
inter alia, under the regulatory provisions for such
charges.
18. Thus, this Tribunal found on the basis of the rival submissions
of the parties that the Appellant has given a binding undertaking on
behalf of all solar power developers in its solar park to bear all the
liabilities related to connectivity/LTA on behalf of these solar power
generators. It appears that for this very reason, the Appellant had
sought deletion of the solar power generators from the array of
respondents in these two appeals which wall allowed by this Tribunal
vide order dated 9th November, 2023. It is to be noted that the
contention of the Appellant that such undertaking was conditional,
has been rejected by this Tribunal upon observing that the
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R.P. No. 2 of 2026 Page 12 of 14

undertaking was given with open eyes, voluntarily and without any
coercion or duress upon understanding the regulatory provisions. It
has also been noted in paragraph No. 97 that an undertaking given
to regulatory authorities for grant of approvals is binding and
enforceable within the regulatory framework of Electricity Act, 2003.
Therefore, we are unable to find any error apparent on the face of
record in the judgement under review on this ground also.
19. To conclude, we may note that upon consideration of all the
relevant contractual provisions as well as statutory provisions and
Regulations, this Tribunal has, in the judgement under review, come
to specific findings on the issues raised in this Review Petition, which
can not be altered in the review proceedings. Well reasoned and well
considered judgement, even though erroneous, does not fall within
the ambit of review. There is a clear distinction between a judgement
suffering from error patent on the face of record and erroneous
judgement. Review Petition is maintainable only on the former case
whereas in the latter case the remedy available to the aggrieved party
is to assail the order/judgement by way of appeal in the higher
forum/Court.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R.P. No. 2 of 2026 Page 13 of 14

20. Manifestly, by way of the instant review petition, the petitioner
is actually seeking a relook of the judgment under review in the hope
to discover any flaw or fault in the same, which is not permissible in
law. The review petition manifestly appears to be appeal in disguise
and thus, does not fall within the scope and ambit of Order XLVII
Rule 1 of the CPC.
21. Hence, we are of the considered opinion that the petitioner has
failed to make out any mistake or error apparent on the face of
record in the judgment under review dated 24th June, 2025 and has
failed to bring the case within the parameters laid down by the
Hon'ble Supreme Court in various decisions on this aspect.
22. The review petition is sans any merit and is accordingly
dismissed.
Pronounced in the open court on this 15th day of September, 2026.
(Ajay Talegaonkar) (Virender Bhat)
Technical Member (Electricity) Judicial Member
